newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts 3.65 pct operational deficit in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts 3.65 pct operational deficit in Jan.

text.p: Brazil posted an operational public sector deficit in January equivalent to 3.65 percent of gross domestic product, the Central Bank said.
The bank said January's result was slightly better than the 3.85 percent of GDP deficit reported in December.
In a statement, the bank said Brazil's monetary base expanded 9.7 percent in February, according to daily averages, or contracted 15 percent in month-on-month terms.
It also said net public sector debt was an estimated 273.61 billion reais in January, representing 34.4 percent of Gross Domestic Product.
In December, Brazil's net debt stockpile stood at 268.77 billion reais, also equivalent to 34.4 percent of GDP.

Brazil's net internal debt in January was 240.78 billion reais, slightly up from December's 237.18 billion reais, while net external debt in January was 32.829 billion reais against 31.59 billion reais in the previous month.
The bank said the public sector posted a tiny primary surplus in January of 0.01 percent of GDP. The primary result, unlike the operational figure, does not include debt servicing costs.
The federal government and the Central Bank posted a 0.29 percent/GDP primary surplus, states and municipalities a 0.48 percent deficit and state-owned companies a 0.2 percent surplus.
The public sector nominal result, which includes debt payments and is adjusted for currency fluctuations, was a 5.84 percent deficit in January, the bank said.
